name: JavaScript
title: JavaScript (ES2025)

type.text: **No static types**: All coupling deferred to runtime
**Prototypes decouple**: Can modify behavior without inheritance
**Duck typing**: Structural at runtime, but no safety
**Coercion follows the operand**: `+` concatenates or adds by the values it receives, so the reader resolves the operand types at the site
String length and indexing are UTF-16 code-unit operations (ECMA-262 6.1.6); charAt can split a surrogate pair

construction.text: **`new` keyword confusing**: `this` binding couples to call context
**Prototype pollution**: Can modify built-in prototypes globally
**One value, many names**: objects and arrays move by reference, so a parameter, a closure, and a property can reach one buffer, and the signature names none of the sharers

memory.text: **Garbage collection decouples memory**: Generational GC (implementation dependent)
**No manual memory management**: Can't have use-after-free
**GC pauses affect latency**: V8, SpiderMonkey, etc. have different characteristics
**Closure captures create leaks**: Easy to accidentally hold references
**Event listener leaks common**: Forgotten listeners prevent collection
**Reference cycles are collected**: A mark-and-sweep collector reclaims objects that point at each other, so a cycle alone is not a leak
**WeakMap/WeakRef help**: Can create weak references, but not automatic
**The class is declared**: type faults are thrown values (documented) catchable at the frame; the engine's own crashes are the implementation's, not the language's

error.text: **Result types possible**: Libraries exist but uncommon
**A callback reports failure beside its value**: the `(err, result)` convention splits one result in two, and the promise path is the one that composes
**The runtime publishes isolation units**: Workers run in their own global scope (documented), and an unhandled fault in a Worker ends the Worker, not the program

concurrency.text: **Single-threaded event loop**: A long task blocks every other callback, so no second core is available for CPU-bound work
**Async functions are explicit**: `async` marks which functions may suspend, so the boundary is visible at the declaration
**Web Workers separate**: Explicit message passing, but manual

platform.text: **No vendor owns the language**: ECMAScript is standardized by Ecma International as ECMA-262 and evolves through the public TC39 proposal process
**Independent engines implement it**: V8, SpiderMonkey, and JavaScriptCore are separate implementations, so a program is not bound to one vendor's runtime
**A runtime exists on every platform**: Every web browser ships an engine, and Node.js, Deno, and Bun run the language outside the browser
**The source is portable between hosts**: The same script runs in a browser and in Node.js; only the host API differs, not the language

performance.text: **Single-threaded**: Couples CPU-bound work to event loop

ecosystem.text: **A node-gyp addon binds to a Node major**: Node promises it only within that major, and the crossing-major path is Node-API [@nodeAbiStability; @nodeNapi]

evolution.text: **ES6 adoption**: Took years to become standard

domain.text: **Excellent for frontend**: Only native browser language

security.text: Every number is an IEEE-754 double: integers above 2^53 change value in silence, and bitwise operators coerce to 32 bits

tradeoffs: **Dynamic `this` vs. the wrapper**: one function can serve several objects without a wrapper, and a method passed as a value needs the caller to bind its context
**Module syntax vs. the loader**: the language states the module form, and the loader that serves it is the platform's
**One language in two hosts**: the same source runs in the browser and on the server, so each host's API surface must be kept apart at the boundary
verdict: JavaScript's dynamic nature defers all coupling detection to runtime. Prototypes and object literals provide flexibility but no guarantees. Global scope and unchecked errors create pervasive coupling. Main strength: object literals and prototypes are simple. Main weakness: no type system means coupling invisible until runtime.

energy.text: Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: A large training corpus and strong code-generation results: models write this language well [@joel2025lowresource; @effibenchx2025].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

use:web-frontend.observation: Every web browser ships an engine

use:web-backend.observation: Node.js, Deno, and Bun run the language outside the browser

roleNote: ES5 (2009) was a browser scripting language; ES2025 (2025) is an application platform with a server runtime. The family's shelf follows its current role, not its origin: this is a role change, not a version change.

delivery.note: The engine parses the source the package ships
Node promises an addon built against one major only within that major, and the crossing-major path is Node-API
Node-API is ABI stable and lets a module built for one major run on later majors
